video_title: Dirk Nowitzki & Steve Nash Talk 90s NBA Fashion + CRAZY All-Time Teammates Starting 5!

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on how Jalen Brunson evolved into an NBA superstar
quotes.excerpt: What are the one, two, three things that changed or that you developed that took you from being a solid NBA player to being a star?

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Nash
text_blocks.text: Jalen, what about from your perspective, what are the one, two, three things that changed or that you developed that took you from being a solid NBA player to being a star?

text_blocks.speaker: Jalen Brunson
text_blocks.text: The one thing I think that changed was the opportunity. I feel like I worked pretty hard. I feel like I was capable of doing things, but sometimes the confidence and opportunity, when that mixes in at the right time, it creates a good mixture to where you are able to think you can do something and actually do something. So, I think the opportunity, but also just the people around me. I think having the teammates I have now that has helped us win together, like also helps it become better.

quotes.speaker: Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.summary_phrase: Dirk Nowitzki on the difficulty of guarding Steve Nash
quotes.excerpt: I knew if I got in his feet, it's uncomfortable. I couldn't contest him anymore.
quotes.quote: When I went to Phoenix and we were playing against each other, obviously neither one of us were known for our defense. So, trying to get him in pick and rolls and attack him was free money. It was a shocker. You know, and sometimes we switched a lot, and actually to be honest with you, I think early I had success guarding him because I could get right underneath him. And then he started to figure out, like, he can use his strength, his size, and then I couldn't contest him anymore. You know, I couldn't make him uncomfortable. So, for me, just trying to be super efficient attacking him, and then we had to change. After a while, I couldn't get under his feet anymore, he turned his back, backed me down to a spot, bumped me off, and shoot over me. Then you have to bring, you know what I mean, now we're not switching anymore. So, like, we had to go go against each other in the playoffs three or four times.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on how the point guard position has evolved
quotes.excerpt: This generation, and the last two, three generations, it's the first line of attack.
quotes.quote: Jalen grew up more in a generation, probably shifted during your childhood, but where when I grew up, point guard, like your dad is a great example, I played against Jalen's dad in the NCAA tournament. He's a great example, classic point guard: run the team, make the passes, score if you need to. That was the generation we grew up for and probably the generation before that. Point guard, run the team, control the team, manage the team, don't shoot a lot and make your shots. And that was the job of a point guard. I think this generation, and the last two, three generations, it's the first line of attack. Why are we waiting around? Try to especially in pace and space, let's try to break the defense down before it gets set and score. So, to me, that number one for our position, I think that just the culture of the game has changed around the position.

quotes.speaker: Jalen Brunson
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson on the shift from running the team to being the primary scorer
quotes.excerpt: It was definitely a shift of like run your team versus like be the first line of attack.
quotes.quote: It was definitely a shift of like run your team versus like be the first line of attack. In high school, my freshman year, I was kind of more like run my team, and then sophomore year, obviously on, it became like the first line of attack and then that's where I felt like I kind of grew. And definitely a shift from like 2012-13 is when I at least I shifted. So within like that five-year span of like 2010 to 2015.

quotes.speaker: Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.summary_phrase: Dirk Nowitzki on the evolution of NBA big men
quotes.excerpt: The evolution of the bigs when we first got in the league, 90s and 90s, the fours and the fives were bigs.
quotes.quote: I would definitely say the skill level of the bigs has been incredible to watch, the evolution of the bigs when we first got in the league, 90s and 90s, the fours and the fives were bigs. If the four could stretch the elbow, that would be a stretch four. I mean, and just rebound our bigs, run a ton of cross screens, and so then the games changed once they started putting in the five-second back-down rule, they put in some zones, so things started shifting. And you know, now it's just everybody has to spread the floor, shoot the ball, bring the ball up, some four-fives initiate offense, bring it up, or the guards are denied, all run the point guard spot for a position or two. So, it's just the skill level, just watch Nikola Jokic can do anything on the court for for bigs, it's just been it's been incredible to watch.

quotes.speaker: Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.summary_phrase: Dirk Nowitzki on his transition to being an NBA analyst
quotes.excerpt: If you would have asked me during my career if I was ever going to be an analyst on TV, I always said you're out of your mind.
quotes.quote: Yeah, it's been super fun. I honestly, if you would have asked me during my career if I was ever going to be an analyst on TV, I always said you're out of your mind. I never wanted to do this and then this opportunity came about and met with met with the bosses and the team and I was all in right away. They're super sweet, they're you know, it feels special to be part of something, you know, you grow from the beginning from scratch and put together, have input. And so it was it's been super fun. It was it was hard and I thought at the beginning, you know, I've been out seven years so the game has changed and the coaches have changed and the players have changed and so I had to kind of dig my way back into it, who's who here even and there were some players that I didn't know and so that was kind of hard for me at the beginning, but these guys make it so easy, obviously Steve just coached, UD and Blake just played a couple years ago, so learn from them, learn from our bosses and it's been it's been super fun.

quotes.speaker: Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.summary_phrase: Dirk Nowitzki praises Nick Van Exel as an all-time teammate
quotes.excerpt: When he was on, Nick the Quick, I mean he was incredible.
quotes.quote: One of my all-time favorite teammates is Nick Van Exel. When he was on, Nick the Quick, I mean he was incredible. That run we had to the Western Conference Finals in '03, he was lights out. He was awesome. Lefty, good throwaway, and when he was hot, he'd throw anything in. Good dude, I love Nick the Quick.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on the difficulty of defending both World Cup and European titles
quotes.excerpt: We're defending World Cup champs and European champs at the same time, doesn't happen very often.
quotes.quote: We're defending World Cup champs and European champs at the same time, doesn't happen very often. That's why I kind of was like, but if I'm honest going forward, they are loaded. If everybody's playing, they're loaded.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash discusses Chelsea's ownership and cheating scandal
quotes.excerpt: Is Chelsea still cheating? The year you won and you were found guilty of cheating, they swept it under the rug.
quotes.quote: Is Chelsea still cheating? The year you won and you were found guilty of cheating, they swept it under the rug because they got rid of the owner.

quotes.speaker: Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.summary_phrase: Dirk Nowitzki reflects on his 2011 championship parade
quotes.excerpt: My dad was at the parade. That's longer than the Knicks drought.
quotes.quote: We won the Europa League two years ago. My dad was at the parade. That's longer than the Knicks drought. Wow.

quotes.speaker: Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.summary_phrase: Dirk Nowitzki discusses his legacy as a one-team player
quotes.excerpt: One team player, best player in franchise history, one of the best international players we've ever had.
quotes.quote: One team player, best player in franchise history, one of the best international players we've ever had, one of the best NBA players we've ever had. Incredible closer, NBA champion for the first time, he brought a championship to Dallas, revolutionized the position. With the perimeter play for a seven-footer, the coordination, movement, he was able to bring the position before he lost it. To me, that's a pretty big legacy. Touched on a lot of points across the game that were groundbreaking.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on his departure from Dallas and the 2006 playoffs
quotes.excerpt: I wanted to stay in Dallas my whole career and was offered a substantially less amount.
quotes.quote: I wanted to stay in Dallas my whole career and was offered a substantially less amount, too much to turn down. I felt like the castoff, like nobody wanted me, the unloved child in a way. And so to play them in the playoffs that year after I left, there was some hot sauce on it. I hit a three, dribble down three, one of those games to win it. It was an important series for me, as much as I didn't like to admit it.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on the differences between international and NBA basketball
quotes.excerpt: The biggest one is the rules. It's a different game.
quotes.quote: The biggest one is the rules. It's a different game. Court's a little smaller, the three-point line's a little closer, there's no three seconds in the lane. The refs also call things differently. You can't put a hand in a face, and there's different things like that. If you flop, you get a warning. So there are things like that, which we're supposed to do in the NBA, we don't really do. So I think right there, that changes the way we play, because you can zone, and there's goal tending. So once the ball hits the rim, you can go over the cylinder and smack it out. So there's a lot of things different.

quotes.speaker: Dirk Nowitzki
quotes.summary_phrase: Dirk Nowitzki on the differences between international and NBA basketball
quotes.excerpt: I saw what Jokic was trying to say and some of the guys got offended.
quotes.quote: I saw what Jokic was trying to say and some of the guys got offended, but I don't think he means they should go over there and learn how to play. I think he means you should see the passion that a EuroLeague game, what's going on. And just because they were asking him also about pressures, like, dude, I played in front of 20,000 people throwing stuff at me. So I think that's more what he meant. But yeah, I agree with Steve, some of the rules are different, the game is different, it's taught a little bit differently.
